_meta.indication: Treatment of uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea due to Neisseria gonorrhoeae in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older, weighing at least 35 kg.

pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, open-label, randomized (2:1), active-controlled, noninferiority trial comparing a single 3 g oral dose of zoliflodacin to a single 500 mg IM dose of ceftriaxone plus a single 1 g oral dose of azithromycin.
pivotal_trials.population: Participants 12 years of age and older, weighing at least 35 kg, with uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea due to N. gonorrhoeae.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Microbiological cure rate at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit (Day 6 ± 2), determined by culture at urethral or cervical sites, in the micro-ITT (urogenital) population.
pivotal_trials.n: 930 patients randomized 2:1; primary analysis micro-ITT (urogenital) population 506 zoliflodacin and 238 control (744 total).
pivotal_trials.result: Microbiological cure rate 90.9% (460/506) for zoliflodacin vs 96.2% (229/238) for control; treatment difference -5.3% (95% CI: -8.6%, -1.4%), meeting the prespecified 12% noninferiority margin.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%) were headache (10% vs 5%), dizziness (3% vs 2%), nausea (3% vs 4%), and diarrhea (2% vs 7%) in the NUZOLVENCE (N=619) vs ceftriaxone/azithromycin (N=308) arms.
target_moa: Zoliflodacin is a first-in-class spiropyrimidinetrione bacterial type II topoisomerase inhibitor that inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, thereby inhibiting bacterial DNA replication.
modality: Small molecule (spiropyrimidinetrione bacterial type II topoisomerase inhibitor).

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions on the role of Nuzolvence in the treatment of uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea.

basis.text: Zoliflodacin has Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation, granted for the treatment of uncomplicated gonorrhea on April 16, 2019.

citations.quote: Zoliflodacin has Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation and underwent Priority Review. The Prescription Drug User Free Act goal date is December 15, 2025.

On February 19, 2019, Entasis submitted requests for QIDP and Fast Track designations to IND 118958 for zoliflodacin granules for oral suspension for the indication of treatment of uncomplicated gonorrhea. The Fast Track designation was granted on April 11, 2019, and the QIDP designation was granted on April 16, 2019.

summary.text: Zoliflodacin was granted Fast Track designation (April 11, 2019) and QIDP designation for uncomplicated gonorrhea (April 16, 2019), and received Priority Review based on its QIDP designation and limited treatment options; it was approved via traditional (non-accelerated) approval as a 505(b)(1) new molecular entity.

(the Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) NDA for zoliflodacin, a spiropyrimidinetrione bacterial type II topoisomerase inhibitor intended to treat uncomplicated gonorrhea due to Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older, weighing at least 35 kg.
